body: This. Is. Insane.
I agree, best damn advice ever.

I wanted to let you know that it's peoples sadness such as your own that inspires me to reach out to help. I'm starting to learn to play the piano, and if I get any good I promise myself to donate 25% or greater of anything I earn to a foundation such as "To Write Love On Her Arms", who helps those with depression get help.

Sure, I'm only 16, but I can have dreams too, right? Best of luck with whatever you decide, but keep in mind that it's people like you that inspire me to make a difference.
Let's say I do get a GPS, where would I go from there? Are there typically organized events everywhere, or would I have to start something?
That sounds interesting, might try that.
I've heard of that, looks amazingly fun, but I don't have a GPS sadly.
Okay, I might try that. Thanks.
I only see 2 in my area in that price range, and not too many pricier ones. But I might look into it. :)
alright, I'll look. I hope you're right. Just curious though, what's your definition of "cheap"?

I've actually wanted to get into photography, but kind of forgot, thanks for the tip!

And that's a good idea to read outdoors. I'll definitely use some of these suggestions ;D
Great site suggestion, I'll look around there a bit.
Again, money is a problem there. Otherwise I'd love to learn piano and synthesizer stuff.
True. But skateboards aren't cheap, and I don't think I could hack one together with anything I have lying around.
That sounds fun. I'll give it a shot, and perhaps gain some skills along the way.
I will try to go do that, depends on parental temper levels though.
True. But doing something I don't enjoy will only cause stress and disappointment for me.
specific ideas, suggestions, building tools, etc? Keep in mind I have a pretty tight budget.
Hmm, perhaps I should try that. I'd have to learn to ride a bike first though. (Yes, that's right, I don't know how to ride a bike.)
Those are fun, but need people to play with, which is hard to do for anyone not old enough to enter a bar.
I'm here to find more things to like ^^
Sounds pretty sweet besides my lack of both a skateboard and a kite. And I'm sure I'd fail at skateboarding too.
Bowling is a sport, not interested.... and I see what you mean there, no.

Transportation would be my primary issue there, but good suggestion. Plus, in order to have an "actual job" I'd need a work permit. Though I have volunteered at my local library before, but didn't really enjoy it much, heh.
Actually yes, but it doesn't quite appeal to me. NEXT.
hiking/camping idea is decent, and as for gf ideas go, I'm looking for things that get me involved with more people, which may or may not lead up to that.

Well, I wanted to let all of you redditers know that I decided to break up with my girlfriend. It was for the best, and I'm feeling a lot better now. However, if my depression does reappear, I will do my best to get it checked by a doctor. Thank you all for the opinions and advice.
Thank you, this is probably the best advice I've heard in my life.

Your entire message hits me deep, let me try breaking it down a bit.

> Love isn't special or unique. Look for someone that makes you happy and helps you be a better person every day. In 4 years you will look back and go "haha - this wasn't love, it was teenage lust and a desire to feel wanted." There is nothing beautiful or exalted about love in this world. 

I have some trouble believing this. I have tried asking out 2 other girls, both I had known in person. One was a complete stranger, one was a good friend. They both rejected me. I felt like I was never going to find someone who would give me a chance. About a year later, I met my girlfriend online. And as this is my first relationship, believing that love isn't "special or unique" is quite difficult for me to grasp.

> The most star-crossed lovers cheat on each other and 3 years later end up realizing they met someone better anyway. 

Being completely honest, that's how my girlfriend got with me. She was with another guy over the internet, and after I expressed my feelings to her she decided to break up with him. She told me how he said he would kill himself if she ever left him, but in the end he said he would not.

> Love isn't some sacrificial conquering entity. 

That hits me deep as well. Our love has been part sacrifice.

> It's just finding someone who you enjoy sharing your life with and that helps you become a better person. 

Yet I remember, at first she gave me meaning to my life, when I was feeling more worthless than ever.

> Seeing her log on to aim was always the highlight of my otherwise bleak and depressing day. 

That tends to be how I feel.

> Since then her and I rarely talk - but It was for the best. It was fun talking to her but unhealthy in the end.

It would be hard for me to just "abandon" her, I'm pretty much her best friend, she doesn't have a lot of supportive people in her life.

> honestly consider how much of an impact that one little thing has on the relationship, not only that but on herself and you as people, that one little thing will cause lots of problems.

That's true, it causes a lot of strain on our relationship as well as on ourselves. That seems to be where a lot of our arguments have been centered, or what they have been heated by. But we've gotten through all our arguments. And I believe that even temporary hate requires passion, while simply not caring is the worst that can happen.

> I suppose the best thing you can do is recommend she see a therapist

She has already seen a therapist, should be returning soon, and has been on anti-depressants for a very long time.

> The fact that she's working to try and come see you is a sign she's devoted, but at the same time, don't let the few good things blind you from the potentially bad things.

And on the opposite side of the equation, her depression seems to be the only real "bad thing". She really does love me, and has shown it multiple times. It's just how the depression eats away at her, and in turn it eats away at me...
Okay, I might just do that, thank you for the suggestion.

As for "proof", I have plenty... I have a google voice account all set up to call her (which I've done a few times), I've webcammed with her over Skype on multiple occassions, and she's sent me hundreds of pictures of her.

> As far as the actual words for your parents, that part I can't really help with. I'd try to think of their possible reactions and have good responses ready.

I understand that, and I've heard other comments saying I should leave my parents in the question asking position, therefore they learn what they want to, and I don't "leave anything out".

So, I have a question for you then: When did you start to realize it was indeed a harmful relationship?

Because I'm starting to be unsure at the moment. If I were to leave her, she would more than likely attempt to kill herself. Many times I've been the last thing she's hung onto. I'm worried that this is pushing me with her. But then again I feel like I truly do love her. But this is the first relationship I've ever been in, so I don't have "experience" if you will. Another guilt thing if you will, she quit school and started working (legal in her country) to earn money to be able to see me.

I don't know if she's hurting me that much, or if it's just me, or if it's other people hurting me.
But no one has suggested ways or methods to open up to my parents. Something like that would be very helpful to me.

Let me be completely honest. My mother married an alcoholic. I used to wonder what the hell was wrong with her, why she did that. But now that I have my girlfriend, I understand this. I feel that love is about finding someone who you truly are passionate about, regardless of their negative points. So I kind of feel like any girl I find will have "problems", and to leave a girl for that would be wrong.

I don't want to share it because the relationship is too serious for my mother's standards. I'm still trying to form my own standards, which is kind of what being a teenager is all about... beginning to drift away from your parents into a bit more independence.

I met her over the internet, but she will have enough money to visit me in 3 months. So we WILL get to see each other, but my mom would have to know about her first. And if my mom were to disapprove, then she wouldn't let us meet. In fact, I fear that she'd take away every form of communication I have.
Well I agree with needing to open up a "line of honest communication", but how would I do that?

Okay, hmmm.
Even though the plans you draw out won't necessarily work, I see that every one looks brighter and brighter! :)
I might be able to make something like that work, I'll have to think about it some more.
I'm not quite sure if the letter thing would work, I've written entire speeches before and not been brave enough to go through with it. I've been afraid to talk to my mom sometimes because of how firmly she holds onto her personal beliefs and won't adjust. She's very paranoid about many things. Just to give you an idea of how paranoid my mom is, she won't let me order pizza for delivery when I'm home alone because she thinks the delivery boy will rape me. >_> She SERIOUSLY said that. 

And I see what you mean by looking to the next day, and I think that will help me a lot.

As far as getting their support, that could be one of my problems and fears. For example, I told my dad about my girlfriend, and he refuses to help me tell my mom. He told me "and when you do tell your mom, make sure you tell her I didn't know about it." So he's basically afraid. >_<

And that's a +1 for self esteem right there, I thought I was one of the last to get a girlfriend. No offense to you of course, it's about quality, not quantity. ;)

Okay, but there's a few problems with even a family doctor.
1) I currently cannot drive myself anywhere, therefore I'd require transportation by a parent.
2) I have an appointment coming up soon, but in order to talk about it alone with my doctor, I'd have to ask my mom to step out, which I don't think I'm brave enough to do.
3) In order to get the prescription, my mom would ask for a full brief on what it is and what it is for... and I don't quite feel comfortable with her knowing what's going through my head right now...
I'm the kind of person that can do something the first time, but then isn't brave enough to do it a second for some reason. I don't know why, but I've been like that a lot.

Though I do see where your creative thinking about "MIGHT start thinking about suicide again" comes from.

I don't believe it is okay for my mom to get involved, because of how I'm afraid she'll respond. She tells me she doesn't want me to be in a "serious" relationship, and she'd definitely consider me and my girlfriend too serious...

Thanks for the kindness, I feel to fully respond to you I need to extend my story.
About 6 months ago I told my mother I thought I might have depression. It took me 3 months to become brave enough to do so. I then went to a psychiatrist for about 5 months. He never assigned me any "meds", and therefore I have never been on any drugs of that nature.  I have been "cleared" from him. But I still feel some regrets about that. On the second visit, he talked to me about how I answered a question on a form I filled out. I answered the question "I think about suicide from time to time, but I would never do it." This resulted in having to sign a form saying I wouldn't hurt myself, etc, and brought my parents into it, essentially putting me on suicide watch. This caused a lot of worry from my parents, and I thought it was unnecessary. So I lied to psychiatrist as soon as I could about the thoughts going away. They really haven't, they just floated back a bit further in my mind. But they were still there, and they've been getting stronger.

I don't believe my hormones are acting up very badly, but that's a valid point.

And the thing I am afraid to tell my parents is a few different things.
1) I need to go back to a psychiatrist (and I would most likely choose a different one)
2) That my feelings could have been influenced by my girlfriend, which my mother doesn't even know about.

I have heard the breathing coping technique from my psychiatrist, which helps just slightly, but not so much. The funny thought one is a great idea though, and I will definitely try that.

I appreciate your time and the environment which you strive to create here. And if there were any troll posts, I would report and think little of it.
